text.title: Growth Loops Worked Example
text.summary: One complete loop spec for a B2B document-sharing viral loop (k 0.13 from three measured stages, 9-day cycle, amplifier multiplier 1.15, 120-day cohort projection with 5 percent saturation per cycle, view-page bottleneck, CAC payback 14.2 to 12.4 months, D30 guardrail within) with a note on each value, plus the same loop as usually drawn and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: A B2B document workspace pays about 310 dollars per new workspace and its payback has slipped past 14 months. Users share documents with people outside their company; some recipients sign up. The event table holds `signup_completed`, `share_sent`, `share_viewed` and `signup_via_share`. The growth team wants to know whether the share loop moves payback and where to work on it.

example.title: external document share loop
example.note: k = 0.45 x 2.4 x 0.12 = 0.13: 45 percent of signups share externally within 14 days, each sharer reaches 2.4 distinct viewers, and 12 percent of viewers sign up; every row carries the query date and sample, so nothing is an assumption (r-stage-conversion-measured-not-estimated, r-loop-efficiency-and-cycle-time). k below 1 makes the loop an amplifier with multiplier 1 / (1 - 0.13) = 1.15, so the projection saturates near 1,000 x 1.15 = 1,150 signups per cycle rather than growing; the cohorts show it approaching that ceiling with 5 percent audience saturation per cycle (r-steady-state-projection-90-days). `signup_via_share` is the fuel-back event: its unit is new signups, the same as the input, and it is the only attribution used for CAC payback (r-loop-closes-output-into-input, r-cac-payback-with-and-without-loop). The view-page conversion at 0.12 is the lowest transition, so it is the bottleneck: doubling it takes k to 0.26 and the multiplier to 1.35, which is why the rank-1 experiment is on the view page and the share prompt at rank 2 needs a written justification (r-friction-map-names-the-bottleneck). The guardrail threshold 0.30 is baseline D30 retention 0.34 minus a 4-point margin; loop-sourced users retain at 0.33, so the loop is not trading quality for volume (r-loop-quality-guardrail). Payback moves from 14.2 to 12.4 months, which answers the question the methodology was invoked for.

example.title: the same loop as usually drawn
example.note: What the validator prints: `loop_type` "viral and content" is not one type (r-one-primary-loop-type); `stage_metrics[0].basis` "benchmark" is neither measured nor assumption and `stage_metrics[1]` is measured with no date or sample (r-stage-conversion-measured-not-estimated); `efficiency.reading` self_sustaining with k 0.6 below 1 and no multiplier (r-loop-efficiency-and-cycle-time); `projection.horizon_days` 30 is below 90, `cycles` 1 below 3, `decay.kind` "none" with rate 0 (r-steady-state-projection-90-days); `friction_map.experiments` is empty (r-friction-map-names-the-bottleneck). Once the schema violations are fixed the cross-field checks add: `stages.fuel_back.unit` "sessions" differs from the input unit "new signups", so the design is a funnel (r-loop-closes-output-into-input); k 0.6 is not the product 0.3 x 2.4 x 0.12 = 0.09; the first cohort already has 300 loop inputs; `cac_payback.attributed_by` "organic" is not the fuel-back event; and the guardrail says within while loop-sourced D30 retention 0.19 is below the 0.30 threshold (r-loop-quality-guardrail).
